description: A DigitalOcean Cloud Firewall that filters traffic to and from one or more of the user's own droplets. Pick this to restrict which ports and addresses can reach a droplet the user already has; find the droplet with list_my_resources. It can't protect anyone else's droplets, databases or buckets.

variables.name: name
variables.label: Name
variables.description: Firewall name: starts with a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63 characters.

variables.name: droplet_request_ids
variables.label: Droplets
variables.description: The request IDs of the user's own droplets to protect, 1 to 5 of them, taken from list_my_resources (a lowercase GUID such as 3f2b8c1e-5d4a-4e6f-9a7b-1c2d3e4f5a6b). Only droplets the user requested and that are provisioned are accepted. Never use a droplet name, a DigitalOcean droplet ID or a tag.

variables.name: inbound_rules
variables.label: Inbound rules
variables.description: Traffic allowed in, 1 to 20 rules; everything else inbound is blocked, including SSH unless a rule allows tcp port 22. Each rule is a protocol, a port range and the source addresses allowed. For SSH, suggest the user's own IP as x.x.x.x/32; 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 (anywhere) are accepted but say that this opens the port to the whole internet.

items.description: One allow rule for incoming traffic.

properties.name: port_range
properties.label: Ports
properties.description: One port (22), a range low-high (8000-9000) within 1-65535, or all. Use all for icmp, which has no ports.

properties.name: source_addresses
properties.label: From
properties.description: 1 to 10 IPv4 or IPv6 CIDRs allowed to connect: 203.0.113.7/32 for one IPv4 address, 2001:db8::/32 for an IPv6 block, 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 for anywhere.

variables.name: outbound_rules
variables.label: Outbound rules
variables.description: Traffic allowed out, at most 20 rules; everything else outbound is blocked. Leave this out to allow all outbound traffic (tcp, udp and icmp to anywhere), which is what most users want: with no outbound rules the droplet can't reach package mirrors or DNS. Each rule is a protocol, a port range and the destination addresses allowed.

items.description: One allow rule for outgoing traffic.

properties.name: port_range
properties.label: Ports
properties.description: One port (443), a range low-high (8000-9000) within 1-65535, or all. Use all for icmp, which has no ports.

properties.name: destination_addresses
properties.label: To
properties.description: 1 to 10 IPv4 or IPv6 CIDRs the droplet may connect to: 203.0.113.7/32 for one IPv4 address, 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 for anywhere.

outputs.name: status
outputs.description: DigitalOcean's status for the firewall: waiting, succeeded or failed.

outputs.name: target_tags
outputs.description: The droplet tags the firewall applies to: rp-<requestId> for each protected droplet request.
